title: The legacy rational scalar extension along the identity coefficient map has a natural unit isomorphism
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $Y$, without a structure map to $k$. Let $\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}$ be the full subcategory of the completed integral module derived category consisting of derived-complete objects whose reductions modulo every positive uniformizer power are finite-torsion constructible with cohomology in one finite interval independent of the power [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Use precisely the presentation $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegralCategory}(D,\ell,\ell
e p,E,Y)$ and the reduction functors $\mathrm{integralDerivedReduction}$. Let $C_E^{\mathrm{old}}=\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}[1/\varpi_E]$ be its raw Hom scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], namely $\mathrm{rationalConstructibleCategory}(D,\ell,\ell
e p,E,Y)$. Let $U_E:C_E^{\mathrm{old}}	o C_E^{\mathrm{old}}$ be the actual functor $\mathrm{rationalScalarExtension}(D,\ell,\ell
e p,E,Y,E,\mathrm{AlgHom.id})$, namely completed integral self-extension followed by raw rationalization. Then there exists a natural isomorphism $u_E:U_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{C_E^{\mathrm{old}}}$. No identification with a different integral constructibility predicate is assumed.

proof.text: Put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. Ordinary derived extension along $R\xrightarrow{1}R$ has a natural multiplication isomorphism $m_K:K\otimes_R^LR\xrightarrow{\sim}K$: on a K-flat representative $P$ it is $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The tensor relation gives $(rx)\otimes1=x\otimes r$, so both composites are identities. These formulas commute with restrictions and differentials, hence give sheaf-complex isomorphisms. They commute with every map of representatives and with the quasi-isomorphisms inverted in derived change of rings, giving the asserted natural derived isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; tensor definition in sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product. The multiplication calculation is elementary.

proof.text: Let $T$ be the actual completed integral self-extension restricted to $\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}$, so its raw rationalization is $U_E$. Every underlying $K$ is derived complete by the stated legacy predicate. Apply the finite-free completed-scalar comparison with $L=E$ and the identity inclusion: its natural isomorphism is $\chi_K:K\otimes_R^LR\xrightarrow{\sim}T(K)$, with exactly the strict reduction tower used by the actual integral scalar extension. Define $t_K=m_K\circ\chi_K^{-1}:T(K)\to K$, with inverse $\chi_K\circ m_K^{-1}$. Both objects already belong to the legacy full subcategory; therefore these ambient arrows are arrows of that full subcategory, and their inverse and naturality equations hold there unchanged. This gives $t:T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A_E^{\mathrm{old}}}$. No change of constructibility predicate is involved.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12, Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, pp. 22-24; apply the existing finite-free comparison in its identity case. Actual legacy functor formulas: lean/Sheaf/Paper/RationalizationKaroubi.lean:133-153.

proof.text: Raw rationalization has the same objects. Define $(u_E)_K=1\otimes t_K$ and $(u_E^{-1})_K=1\otimes t_K^{-1}$. For an integral arrow $f:K\to L$ and scalar $a\in E$, the specified identity coefficient map makes $U_E(a\otimes f)=a\otimes T(f)$; in the actual localization coordinates this uses $\mathrm{rationalCoefficientEquiv}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}(\mathrm{rationalCoefficientEquiv}(a)))=a$. Thus $ (u_E)_L\circ U_E(a\otimes f)=a\otimes(t_L\circ T(f))=a\otimes(f\circ t_K)=(a\otimes f)\circ(u_E)_K$. Additivity extends this equality to all localized arrows, which are finite sums of pure tensors. Bilinear composition gives both inverse equations from $t_Kt_K^{-1}=1$ and $t_K^{-1}t_K=1$. Hence these components define the required natural isomorphism $u_E:U_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{C_E^{\mathrm{old}}}$.
